_readme: Seed traveler histories and abandoned carts for the Windfall recovery demo.
Synthetic by choice, for the two reasons in paper section 3.2.3: real booking
records are personally identifiable, and the penyisihan rules require static
parameters. Distribution shape is calibrated against Hotel Booking Demand
(Antonio, de Almeida & Nunes, 2019).
ABOUT valueIdr. These are the prices AT ABANDONMENT -- what the traveler was
looking at when they walked away. They are historical fact about the cart, not
a live quote, which is why they belong here.
That distinction is load-bearing. p_0 in delta_k = (p_0 - p_k)/p_0 is the
abandonment price. If p_0 were a fresh re-quote, rung 01 (re-price the same
cart) would compare the current price to itself and could only ever return 0%,
which would silently disable the cheapest rung on the ladder.
WHAT IS STILL NOT IN HERE: rung prices and outcomes. Those come from live
re-query and from the decision core respectively. A seed that pre-assigned an
outcome would make the demo a slideshow.
calibrationTarget is a seed-DESIGN goal, not a pipeline input. Nothing reads it
at runtime. It records which path each traveler was constructed to exercise so
that capture can check live prices actually produce it, and fail loudly when
they do not.
PROVENANCE. The ten travelers, their names, routes, carriers, hotels, dates,
campaign shares, budget gaps, abandonment times and target outcomes are taken
from the design bundle's seed() table (Windfall.dc.html).
What could NOT be taken verbatim: the bundle's own cart values contradict its
own tier labels -- its lowest-spending traveler is labelled Comfort while
higher-spending ones are labelled Value, which no percentile tiering can
produce. usualSpend is therefore chosen so the bundle's tier AND its budget
gap both fall out of the real arithmetic: p_0 = usualSpend * (1 + gap), and
the percentile rank over these ten lands each traveler on the bundle's tier.
